quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle at night, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distances. You need at least three seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. This gives you extra time to notice if the vehicle stops and time to slow down or stop safely.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign?

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: First, stop where the stop sign is. Then you can move forward slowly and stop again just before entering the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around any buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while you look.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of a crash?

options.text: Keep other drivers from knowing what you plan to do.
Always stay within one foot of another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Stay visible to other drivers at all times. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and always look ahead, behind, and to the sides of your bike.

questions.question: What should you do if you cannot avoid riding on a slippery road?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to keep your balance.
Not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.
questions.explanation: Try to avoid slippery roads completely. If you cannot avoid one, keep your motorcycle upright and ride as slowly as possible.

questions.question: What best protects your eyes from wind while riding?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Most windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Be ready to change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should you position yourself in the lane?

options.text: Always avoid the left portion of the lane.
Always avoid the right portion of the lane.
Always avoid the center portion of the lane.

questions.explanation: There is no single lane position to always avoid. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works correctly.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding, check the controls and learn the gear pattern. Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before you start riding.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front of the group. This way, experienced riders at the back can watch over them.

questions.question: Your body removes about one alcoholic drink per hour. A person drinks seven drinks in three hours. How many drinks will likely still be in their system three hours after their last drink?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. A person who drinks seven drinks in three hours will have about four drinks left in their system three hours later.

questions.question: In most motorcycle crashes, the riders are:

options.text: Riding for hours before the crash.
On a trip longer than 30 miles.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen when riders travel slower than 30 mph. Most crashes occur on short trips of less than five miles.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle best, a rider should:

options.text: Use arms to hold their body up.
Keep knees away from the gas tank.
Keep feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your arms should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to stay balanced.

questions.question: To stop quickly on wet pavement, you should:
questions.explanation: Use both brakes for a quick stop on slippery surfaces. Apply the front brake slowly to prevent it from locking up.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly and stay straight. Slowly brake only on the good tire. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use your high beam light, if possible.

questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, reduce speed and increase your following distance. Use headlights of other vehicles to see ahead. Use your high beam, except when meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up in a wobble—it makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble. Slowly close the throttle to slow down. Lean forward and down. Pull off the road when safe.

questions.question: A helmet will not provide the best protection if:

options.text: It is certified by the DOT.

questions.explanation: A helmet must meet DOT and state standards, fit snugly, and have no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps for full protection.

questions.question: Which of the following is not important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no obvious defects, such as cracks or loose padding.

questions.explanation: Check that your helmet meets DOT and state standards, fits snugly all around, and has no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's total braking power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 75 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to create distance between you and the tailgater.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make the danger worse by encouraging them to follow you faster.

questions.question: What type of sign can be rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular. They are white with black lettering or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When riding on slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden moves, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It uses less space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is less likely to be separated.
The riders will arrive faster in a close group than in a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: The riders will arrive faster in a close group than in a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a close group is better because it uses less space, is easier to see, and is less likely to be separated at traffic lights. However, close riding does not make you arrive faster.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog is chasing you?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.
